iterations.theme: Introductory part of the show, discussion about patriotism and the host's opening greetings

sections.subtitle: Fragmented beginning: call for vaccination and the first lines of the conversation
sections.screenshot_description: Shot from the beginning of the show showing the show title and the first participants of the conversation in the studio, with subtitles displaying the first lines about vaccination.
sections.content:
The first few minutes of the show are marked by a recording of poor quality and a very disconnected automatic transcript, which makes some of the lines difficult to reconstruct reliably. Even so, from the legible parts it can be made out that the conversation from the very start revolves around vaccination and trust in experts.

One of the participants (labelled in the transcript as SPEAKER_01, without an officially stated role) calls on fellow citizens, especially the elderly, to understand the importance of vaccination. In doing so, he mentions a new slogan which, according to his words, appeared at Saturday protests: „Misli na sebe, ugrozi druge” ("Think of yourself, endanger others"). Immediately afterwards he asks why people do not trust our experts.

A second participant (SPEAKER_04) speaks in short, fragmentary lines about testing vaccines on children. He points out that many vaccines, according to his words, are developed in Western countries, but that they were tested in poor areas of Asia and Africa. He concludes that testing must also be carried out on children in Europe and America, and not only in Africa and Asia, so that parents can be sure of the vaccine's safety.

In the same part of the show, an excerpt from a political interview also appears. A government representative, Radić (SPEAKER_05, listed in the official list as Guest 4), talks about the effect of introducing the euro on prices. According to his words, based on the experience of other member states, prices rose on average by only 0.23 percent, which for one coffee would mean an increase of about two lipa. He lists as the government's priorities demographic revitalization, the green transition and digital transformation, and investment in education.

In the part that follows, Radić rejects the possibility of introducing a property tax, which, in his interpretation, was not part of the election programme. The interlocutor (SPEAKER_06, Guest 5) asks him about this directly and addresses him as „gospodina Radića” ("Mr Radić"), and repeats that a property tax is not planned, since ownership should not be taxed retroactively. Radić replies that this is not an option and that the goal is gradually to shift the burden from taxing labour to taxing property.

sections.subtitle: Discussion about patriotism: „Hrvati se fure da vole Hrvatsku” ("Croats pretend to love Croatia")
sections.screenshot_description: The speaker in the frame talks while the on-screen subtitle reads „Što je za tebe domoljublje?” ("What is patriotism to you?"), and speaker 3 sits opposite.
sections.content:
After the introductory fragments, the conversation turns to the question of the relationship to the homeland. The speaker (SPEAKER_00, Guest 2) claims that people in Croatia simply do not love their country, unlike, as he puts it, Germans, English and French, who, according to his words, adore their state.

The speaker claims that Croats only „furaju” ("pretend") to love Croatia, while in reality, in his opinion, people are plundering their own country. To this, speaker 3 (SPEAKER_19, Guest 3) remarks that everyone thinks Croats are the greatest patriots. Guest 2 rejects this by asking how someone who steals from his own brother Croat can be a patriot, and concludes that he does not see patriotism in that.

Guest 3 then asks the key question: „Što je za tebe domoljublje?” ("What is patriotism to you?"). Guest 2 replies that patriotism is loving one's country, stressing that he loves Croatia and does not want to destroy it, but rather to contribute and create. He additionally stresses that such an attitude, in his opinion, does not develop among us as it does in France, where, as he says, people have an ingrained sense of the state.

The discussion ends with the indignant assessment that the situation is „užas” ("horror") and the speaker's conclusion that the nation is what it is and that it will take many years for the situation to change. It is important to note that the claims that „Hrvati ne vole svoju zemlju” ("Croats do not love their country") were presented as the speaker's personal assessment, without data or research to support them.

sections.subtitle: The host opens the show with a greeting and a link to Vinkovci
sections.screenshot_description: The host in the studio, in the foreground, greets viewers against a background with the logo of the channel „Bez dlake na glavi” ("Without a hair on the head").
sections.content:
After the discussion about patriotism, the host (SPEAKER_20) opens tonight's show with the greeting „dobra večer, dragi ljudi” ("good evening, dear people"). He points out that he presents himself as a native of Vinkovci, and that in the opening minutes of the gathering he should not miss a tribute to a deceased musician, thereby announcing the next topic.

The host talks about his rhythm and tempo, and from his opening words it is clear that he intends to run the show with many personal comments, without a strict structure. Along the way he refers to a speech which, according to his words, was given earlier in the gathering, and stresses that „ovdje puno prije njega” ("here, long before him") someone talks about right-wing people.

In this part the host does not present new data, but establishes the tone of the show: personal memories, comments about public figures and direct address to viewers, with an announcement that he will deal „na prvom mjestu” ("first and foremost") with musical and social topics.

sections.subtitle: Tribute to Goran Bare: a musician who, according to the host, „pogađao tamo gdje boli” ("hit where it hurts")
sections.screenshot_description: Archive photograph or a shot of a concert performance, with the subtitle „Goran Bare – omaž” ("Goran Bare – tribute"), while the host talks about the musician.
sections.content:
The host lingers for some time on the tribute to the frontman of the band Majke, Goran Bare. According to his words, Bare also performed in the campaign of Račan and Budiša, and later, as the host says, was musically connected with political topics too, so some portrayed him as a „komunjara” ("commie") and a „jugonostalgičar” ("Yugo-nostalgic").

The host claims that Bare spoke about so-called weekend right-wingers, that is, those who loudly swagger and do not represent „prave ljude koji vole svoju domovinu” ("real people who love their homeland"). Such a sentence serves the host as an introduction to the conclusion that real love of the homeland does not need to be loud, but shows itself through deeds and attitude towards the people.

In the same segment the host also mentions Dino Dvornik, about whom, as he says, people often speak in an insulting way, including claims about addiction. The host stresses that Dvornik was a „primjer koji nikad nije bježao od toga” ("an example who never ran away from it") and that he himself spoke about the consequences of drugs, quoting him in the sense of: „pogledajte mene i vidite što mi je to od života napravilo” ("look at me and see what that has made of my life").

The host concludes that the tribute is a duty to a musician who, in his opinion, was sharp and hit where it hurts, although some did not understand him. He stresses that today, as he says, the world would miss such a voice.

sections.subtitle: Announcement of the 207th gathering: from space to Croatia and European topics
sections.screenshot_description: Title card of the show with the serial number 207 and a list of announced topics (space, viruses, Croatia, Europe).
sections.content:
The host formally greets the audience on the channel „Bez dlake na glavi” and announces the 207th live gathering. He announces that the conversation will move „od svemira do Hrvatske, preko virusa do nekih europskih tema” ("from space to Croatia, through viruses to some European topics"), and stresses that the show's cover is linked to a certain woman from a piece of content that will be addressed towards the end.

As a point of interest, the host announces a segment about Donald Trump and Mike Tyson, which he claims will be a „biser” ("gem") for viewers. He also announces that at the end of the show he will address a topic which, as he says, viewers more experienced than him already know well, and mentions a cult film from the eighties about glasses that reveal the real picture of the world beneath propaganda.

The host stresses that the show is thematically diverse, but that certain topics will build on one another. This announcement shows the structure of the evening: from the introductory part about space, through health and political topics, to the concluding segment.

sections.subtitle: Thanks to viewers and subscribers: „Vi ste sponzor onoga što radim” ("You are the sponsor of what I do")
sections.screenshot_description: Screen with a list of names of viewers from the chat and a note of thanks for support, with visible subscriber markers.
sections.content:
In this part of the show the host thanks the many viewers who sent greetings and comments through the chat. He reads a series of names and greetings (such as Mojca, Vedran, Alfred, Renata and others), and some of these names he recognises with a certain degree of uncertainty because of the quality of the transcript.

He especially stresses the financial support of the audience. He points out that, alongside advertisements, viewers are his only real sponsor of the content, and invites those who can to support the channel through subscriptions, payment into an account or donations. Along the way he mentions that the show, because of its length, requires a lot of preparation and that it may last up to three hours.

The host expresses gratitude to everyone who contributes to his work „na bilo koji način” ("in any way"), with the note that without this support he would not be able to devote time to preparation, translation and processing of material.

sections.subtitle: The channel's fifth anniversary: from the first video to six hundred pieces of content
sections.screenshot_description: Shot showing the number of years (5) and the display of the channel's first video from the archive, with the highlighted title „Peta godišnjica” ("Fifth anniversary").
sections.content:
The host announces that the channel celebrates its fifth birthday in three days, and that five years have passed since the first video. As the beginning he cites a video in which he talked about topics related to a cold and the corona virus, with mention of certain medicines, and since then, as he says, the channel has published about 600 videos.

The host stresses that some people from the beginning of the channel have survived and that, according to his words, they survived „nevjerojatne” ("incredible") pressures and forecasts. He claims that many television personalities of that time, in his opinion, frightened and terrorised the public, while, as he says, they were „u biti bili trgovački putnici farmakomafije” ("basically travelling salesmen of the pharma-mafia").

The statement is presented as the host's personal assessment, without concrete evidence, and it is important to stress that such generalisations about the media and pharmaceuticals cannot be verified from this part of the conversation. Nevertheless, through this recapitulation a clear continuity of critical attitude towards official health institutions can be seen, which characterises the entire show.

sections.subtitle: Space: the death of an engineer, „izgubljeni papiri” ("lost papers") and astronauts at the centre of doubts
sections.screenshot_description: Photograph or archive shot of an astronaut crew from a space mission, with a subtitle about the death of an engineer and the lost NASA documents.
sections.content:
The first topic of the show is space. The host reports that a woman whose code was crucial for the first landing of humans on the Moon has died. He shows her photograph with a bundle of papers and claims that NASA, according to his claim, lost those papers, and probably the seals that were on them.

The host then raises the suspicion that there was a loss of technology and documentation, referring to the fact that the capabilities of the technology of the time, which, according to his words, was small enough to fit in a calculator, have today far surpassed it. Along the way he criticises the fact that, as he says, the United States is again announcing a trip to Mars, although, in his opinion, it has lost part of its own past.

Further on, the host talks about astronauts on the International Space Station and expresses an ironic assessment of international cooperation in space, with the comment that there are representatives of different countries among the crew members. He especially mentions a female astronaut who, according to his words, spent the longest time in space and who, after returning, allegedly forgot how to walk, which she attributed to the loss of gravity.

The host does not connect that statement with verifiable medical data, but uses it for broader claims about „montirani” ("staged") scenes from space. He also speculates that the cameraman of the return from the Moon is allegedly „još uvijek tamo” ("still there"), which is presented as a joke, but also as an example of conspiracy theories which, as he says, circulate on the internet.

It is important to note that these claims cannot be supported by evidence from the transcript, and some names and details are unclear because of the quality of the transcription.

sections.subtitle: Plague in Siberia: a report from Russia and geopolitical interpretations
sections.screenshot_description: News shot or a map of Siberia with the caption „Kuga u Sibiru” ("Plague in Siberia"), with ambulances in front of a hospital.
sections.content:
After the space topic, the host moves on to news from Russia. He reports that the plague in Siberia, according to reports, has gotten out of control and that the disease has entered hospitals, noting that emergency services are tracking the movement of vehicles.

The host then sets up a geopolitical framework: he claims that part of the public will see Russia as the „dobra strana” ("good side") alongside Iran and China, while Russia, in his opinion, shows itself to be „štreberski” ("nerdishly") orderly in reporting cases. This claim remains at the level of a personal comment without a source.

The host also speculates that a new pandemic could come after changes of power in the United States, and links the elections with a possible „klatno” ("pendulum") in global politics. Here the discussion increasingly moves towards predictions that have no support in verified facts, which continues in the next part of the show.

For the purposes of this overview, it is important to point out that the report on the plague in Siberia is presented in the transcript as news, but that its subsequent interpretations are the host's, not the result of verified sources.

sections.subtitle: Theories about new viruses: bats, „inflacija virusa” ("virus inflation") and 11 thousand unknown pathogens
sections.screenshot_description: Illustration of a bat and a display of a virus under a microscope, with the graphic caption „11.000 nepoznatih virusa” ("11,000 unknown viruses").
sections.content:
In the part about pandemics the host presents a series of speculative theses. He claims that „virus čeka u kutu” ("a virus is waiting in the corner") and that after a new change in American politics a new pandemic will probably come. In doing so he lists possible sources: a bat, a badger, a dolphin, a snail or even a spider from a zoo, which he presents as a series of random possibilities without a source.

The host claims that, according to his words, around 11 thousand viruses have been discovered on the bottom of the Pacific Ocean, almost all of them unknown, and warns that one of them could „iskočiti” ("jump out"). He also states that, according to his interpretation, coronaviruses were described in biology textbooks from the seventies as causes of colds, and that only later were they presented as „novi” ("new"), which, according to his claim, made it possible to apply extraordinary measures.

The host also brings in an analogy with inflation: he claims that central banks „printaju” ("print") money without backing, and that it is similar with viruses, whose „inflation” could reduce their value but increase their number. Along the way he suggests that viruses could also be biological weapons, with alleged radiation and other invisible factors, without citing a source.

Further on the host ironically describes his own role, saying that he is „onaj koji ide korak dalje” ("the one who goes a step further") and that he does not believe in some earlier claims either, but still advocates scepticism towards official explanations.

Because of such claims it is key to stress that the transcript contains no evidence for the speculation about biological weapons, about 11 thousand „unknown” viruses, or about hidden intentions in explaining the coronavirus.

sections.subtitle: Suspension of vaccines for newborns: a call for caution and a quoted article
sections.screenshot_description: Screenshot of an article with a headline about suspending vaccines for newborns and a quote about symptoms, with the host reading the text.
sections.content:
The host moves on to a topic he describes as „ozbiljniju” ("more serious"): the urgent suspension of vaccines for newborns and the rise in reports of side effects. He reads an excerpt from an article which states that symptoms may appear from several months to several years after vaccination, most often after a year, with the claim that full recovery is achieved with timely diagnosis and treatment.

The host comments on this sentence ironically, suggesting that the article, in his opinion, does not clearly enough state that the vaccine is not safe and effective. He stresses that it is important to notice the time range in which symptoms may appear, and asks whether this could explain later health conditions.

The host also mentions that the article itself, according to his claim, was taken from another source and quotes an expert, but the exact data about the source and context of the quote are not entirely clear from the transcript. In the comments a comparison of the vaccine with „otrov za štakore” ("rat poison") also appears, which the host puts forward as a metaphor for delayed consequences, but without evidence.

It is clear from this point of the show that the focus is on the way the data is presented: the host suggests that the consequences have been „elegantno” ("elegantly") presented as side effects, which, in his opinion, is wrong.

sections.subtitle: Criticism of reporting side effects: „posljedice” ("consequences") instead of „nuspojave” ("side effects") and the story about Minister Beroš
sections.screenshot_description: Shot in which the host speaks with the subtitle „Posljedica, a ne nuspojava” ("Consequence, not side effect"), while a graphic with the institution's mark is visible in the background.
sections.content:
The host continues his criticism of the way side effects of vaccines are reported. He claims that parents are discouraged from reporting side effects after a few months, because, according to his words, health workers often do not accept them even after a few days. Instead of the term „nuspojava” ("side effect"), he proposes the term „posljedica” ("consequence"), which he considers more precise.

He then mentions an alleged statement by Minister Beroš, which, according to his words, he is quoting from a recorded conversation in front of the KBC Rebro building. The host claims that when asked how many „lasta” ("swallows") are needed for a vaccine to be suspended, the minister replied: „više od jedne” ("more than one"). The host thereby suggests that the minister knowingly ignored safety risks, but the recording is not shown in this part of the show and is announced for some future broadcast.

The host also links the vaccine with health problems in children, such as anxiety and depression, and claims that during the pandemic parents were exposed to pressure to isolate their children. These claims are not supported by data in this part of the transcript.

In the end the host advocates that the protection of children be ensured through supervision and responsibility, with an expression of concern that vaccines are still being administered in 2026.

sections.subtitle: Protest in Split and calls for the „zlatna sredina” ("golden mean")
sections.screenshot_description: Portal front page with the headline „U Splitu prosvjed zbog obustave cijepljenja beba protiv tuberkuloze” ("In Split a protest over the suspension of vaccinating babies against tuberculosis").
sections.content:
In this part the host refers to the headline about a protest in Split concerning the suspension of vaccinating children against tuberculosis. He asks viewers what first comes to mind when they read such a headline, and says that he himself wonders whether parents will really go out to protest over a vaccine.

According to his description, the association that organised the protest deals, among other things, with the right of parents to choose and with questionable products, but without clear answers to questions about safety. The host stresses that articles about the protest, in his opinion, cannot be fully understood without a broader context.

In conclusion the host takes a position in favour of the „zlatna sredina” ("golden mean"): neither full vaccination nor full opposition, but a decision by parents with full information. He repeats that it would be better for people to be told the „potpuna istina” ("full truth"), including the question of the growing number of children with learning difficulties and disorders, which, in his opinion, was not the case earlier.

This conclusion remains at the level of the host's opinion, without empirical data in the transcript that would confirm a link between vaccination and these disorders.

sections.subtitle: Criticism of the medicines agency and announcement of a video contribution
sections.screenshot_description: The host in the studio announces a video contribution, with a graphic titled „Ekskluzivno: provjera kakvoće cjepiva” ("Exclusive: checking the quality of vaccines") and a four-minute duration marker.
sections.content:
Towards the end of this part of the show the host criticises the Agency for Medicinal Products and Medical Devices (HALMED), claiming that, in his opinion, this institution performs mostly a formal role and „lupa pečat” ("stamps") decisions that others have already made. He stresses that its job description should include control and regulation, but that, in his judgement, this is not visible in practice.

The host then announces a video contribution that will show „ekskluzivne” ("exclusive") information about checking the quality of vaccines on the market of the Republic of Croatia. He announces that the video lasts about four minutes and that he has no intention of interrupting it. This announces the next part of the show, in which an official inquiry and the agency's response will be read.

For the purposes of this iteration it is important to record that this part of the show contained sharp criticism of institutions and an announcement of a document whose content is shown in the transcript only later. It is therefore crucial to check the content of the contribution before drawing any conclusions.

iterations.theme: Vaccine safety, medicines agency controls and Croatian social and economic topics

sections.subtitle: Official inquiry that revealed a gap in vaccine oversight
sections.screenshot_description: Guest 1 reads an official inquiry from a parents' association to the Agency for Medicinal Products and Medical Devices, with the text shown on screen.
sections.content:
The show moves to a video contribution in which Guest 1 reads an official inquiry that was sent to the Agency for Medicinal Products and Medical Devices on behalf of a parents' association of activists. Guest 1 introduces the topic by pointing out that many people believe that the contents of vaccines used in Croatia are regularly checked, similar to inspections of food, toys or cosmetics, which often lead to products being withdrawn from the market.

An additional reason for the inquiry, according to Guest 1's words, was the great interest of the public in the topic of vaccination and vaccine safety over the last few months. Since the Agency has in its job description ensuring the safety and quality of medicines, vaccines and medical devices on the market, the association posed two specific questions.

- Is there a laboratory at the Agency where analysis of the contents of vaccine vials can be carried out and, if so, what is its capacity?
- Was analysis of the contents of vaccine vials carried out in the last five years, and do reports on those analyses exist?

sections.subtitle: The Agency's response: a laboratory exists, but not a single analysis in five years
sections.screenshot_description: Display of the Agency's official response, or Guest 1 summarising the response, with a caption about the key message.
sections.content:
According to Guest 1, an official response from the Agency arrived shortly afterwards. From it, it follows that a laboratory for checking medicines exists at the Agency, but that in the last five years not a single analysis checking the contents of vaccine vials has been carried out.

The host reacts to this at 00:44:00 and expresses support for the association for the honesty of the answer, and talks about what, in his opinion, the Agency actually does. He asks what the purpose is of an institution whose employees, as he claims, are paid to „lupe pečat” ("stamp") a finished decision made by others. He points out that the Agency's job description includes regulating the market, but that in practice, in his assessment, checks are not carried out. The host stresses that he is not against vaccines as such, but advocates completely voluntary vaccination, in which the parent decides for themselves.

The host also gives an assessment of the salary of the Agency's employees („nekoliko tisuća eura neto” ("several thousand euros net")), but this claim is not supported by data in the transcript.

sections.subtitle: Administrative checking instead of real oversight
sections.screenshot_description: Guest 1 explains the vaccine approval procedure, with a graphic showing the term „administrativna provjera” ("administrative check").
sections.content:
Guest 1 further explains how the procedure works. When approving a vaccine for the market, the Agency carries out exclusively an administrative check of documentation. One of the documents is a certificate of vaccine quality issued by a laboratory within the European Union, and the Agency accepts such a certificate. Guest 1 stresses that part of the audience does not perceive this as a problem, but that probably a large number of people were under the wrong impression that strict controls are regularly carried out.

At 00:46:54 the host summarises the same message: in the last five years, he says, the result is zero. He then comments that he trusted even the experts who had appeared earlier in his shows, despite the fact that, according to his words, there were also some who had „zakačili” ("hooked") his topic.

Guest 1 concludes that the entire correspondence, including the inquiry and the Agency's response, is available on the website Cijepljenje.info, so anyone can review the documents themselves. The host continues ironically that the Agency, it seems, did not even fabricate false analyses, which, he says, would at least not be honest, and again asks what purpose such an institution serves.

sections.subtitle: A story about a doctor and the claim about „nehumano” ("inhumane") monitoring of side effects
sections.screenshot_description: The host speaks in the frame, with a caption bearing the name of the doctor Alma Demirović.
sections.content:
The host then moves on to a personal story linked to the doctor Alma Demirović. According to his words, she publicly spoke about her own experience in which her child, according to her claims, suffered after a vaccine. The host claims that he had the honour of meeting this doctor and that she described the „horor” ("horror") she went through while trying to prove something she herself had experienced.

The host also cites an alleged statement by the then head of the agency about whether doctors record all side effects. According to his version, it was said that this would be too much work and would be „nehumano” ("inhumane"). He concludes that for this reason a child who has been harmed by a vaccine could often find it difficult to express pain, which, in his opinion, would show the baseness of the system.

It is important to note that these claims are presented solely in the form of the host's retelling and personal interpretation, and are not supported by documents in the transcript. In the same passage the host also mentions other doctors, such as Nada Jurinčić and Lidija Gajski, but does not give their specific statements.

sections.subtitle: The Split protest and the question of what people actually think about the headline
sections.screenshot_description: On screen the headline of the media article „U Splitu prosvjed zbog obustave cijepljenja beba protiv tuberkuloze” ("In Split a protest over the suspension of vaccinating babies against tuberculosis"), while the host speaks.
sections.content:
At 00:50:40 the host moves on to the topic of the protest in Split over the suspension of vaccinating newborns against tuberculosis. He announces that the media will „ubaciti” ("insert") the headline into the conversation and asks viewers to say without filtering what first comes to mind when reading the headline: why people are going to protest.

The host admits that, after reading the article, he thought that parents were really protesting against a vaccine which, as he claims, they themselves admitted was not good. After that, he says, he looked for information on the websites of the association that organised the protest. He concludes that the association deals with topics in which a parent has the right to say that certain products are „blago rečeno upitni” ("putting it mildly, questionable"), which, according to his words, is fine.

In the same segment the host also expresses his own view that the problem of autism and learning difficulties, in his assessment, has appeared in schools in the last twenty years or so in far greater numbers than before. These claims are not supported by data in the transcript.

sections.subtitle: Viewers on „banned” natural treatment and linen fabrics for newborns
sections.screenshot_description: The host reads a viewer's comment on screen, with a shot of a linen blanket.
sections.content:
At 00:54:07 the host reads viewers' comments. One of them claims that vaccines are just a continuation, because, allegedly, natural treatments were banned first, and then ointments too, with warnings about cholesterol and restrictions on salt and meat.

The host follows on from this topic and retells a video that a friend sent him. According to that video, flax and linen blankets, which were standard for newborns, have a „visoka frekvencija” ("high frequency") which, as it is claimed, protects the child. The host repeats that this is a layperson's interpretation and describes a „pozitivna frekvencija” ("positive frequency") which, in his interpretation, envelops the child. In the same passage he also mentions old hospitals with sunbathing pools.

No scientific source for this claim exists in the transcript, and the host does not cite a specific document or an expert assessment. The passage shows how the show mixes audience comments, personal beliefs and other people's videos, without checking their credibility.

sections.subtitle: Criticism of the pharmaceutical industry and the „real” face of medicine
sections.screenshot_description: The host speaks in the frame, with captions reading „farmacija” ("pharmacy"), „biznis” ("business") and „Rockefeller”.
sections.content:
At 00:56:00 the host develops a critique of the pharmaceutical industry and modern medicine. He claims that the name Abraham Alexander, which in the transcript he gives as „Abraham Alexander”, is linked to 1910, when, according to his claim, with funding from Rockefeller and Carnegie, he „pretukao” ("beat up") the medicine of the time. That event, he says, is today called alternative medicine, while „prava medicina” ("real medicine") would be the one that developed after it.

The host presents a paradox: despite more and more science and medicines, the number of sick people is rising. From this he draws the claim that pharmacy „drži medicinu” ("holds medicine") because it is a business that survives only if it has consumers, that is, sick people. He draws a comparison with arms manufacturers, such as Lockheed Martin and Rheinmetall, which, according to him, have an interest in tensions and wars.

Such claims are presented as the host's personal opinion and are not accompanied by sources. In the same segment the host also talks about his own experience of a child who hid in a cellar during the Homeland War.

sections.subtitle: Causes of autism: between a single cause and chemicals in the environment
sections.screenshot_description: On screen a comment from viewer Luka about the causes of autism, while the host responds in the frame.
sections.content:
At 00:58:21 the host reads a comment from viewer Luka that concerns the causes of autism. The host, as he himself says, „nepopularno” ("unpopularly") declares that he believes in multiple factors and not in a single cause. He lists chemicals in food, dyes, air, water, poisons and radiation as possible factors, although he does not cite data or studies that would confirm this.

The host stresses that he is not convinced of what Luka states as the source, but that he, as he says, „naslijepo” ("blindly") agrees with him in the part that concerns the environment. He adds that such a thought is not unpopular in his home.

This segment can be seen as an example of how the show combines viewers' natural concern with claims about the environment, without concrete scientific sources in the transcript.

sections.subtitle: Smell in Zagreb and Našice and waste from Gospić
sections.screenshot_description: Shot with an illustration of a smell and a caption about fires in recycling yards; the host speaks about waste from Gospić.
sections.content:
From 00:59:05 the host talks about air pollution. He describes that in Zagreb a „misteriozni smrad” ("mysterious smell") was present for several days, the exact source of which is not known. He offers a guess about a possible combination of waste, with speculation about the involvement of the Agroproteinka plant, without any evidence.

In Našice, according to his words, the smell is the result of frequent fires in recycling yards and at landfills, which he links to climate change. The host further claims that waste from Gospić ended up in a cement plant, which he describes as a decision of the Government for which, in his opinion, there is no adequate place. He describes part of the waste as imported from the „mafije iz Italije” ("mafia from Italy"), a claim without a source.

The host also refers to a previous video contribution in which a female interlocutor spoke about waste from Gospić, and which, according to his words, received more than thirty thousand views. At the same time he also mentions fires in Dalmatia, on Rab and in Pula, which he also links to landfills and the dry season, putting forward the claim of a possible influence of a „kontroverznog poduzetnika iz Zagreba” ("controversial entrepreneur from Zagreb"), without citing a source.

sections.subtitle: Sports facilities as a „lijek” ("cure") for Split: criticism of state policy
sections.screenshot_description: The host comments on news about financing sports facilities in Split, with a display of air conditioners at the railway station.
sections.content:
At 01:03:54 the host moves on to the topic of building sports facilities in Split. He cites news that the Government is giving almost 55 million euros for sports halls and a stadium in Split, which he ironically calls „fantastične vijesti” ("fantastic news"). He recalls the affair around Maksimir and criticises what he calls a short-sighted approach.

The host also comments on the architecture of Split's buildings, including the railway station and the bus station, which, he says, mix Dalmatian authenticity and modern elements, that is, the air conditioners differ according to period. He claims that the bus station has remained consistent with the legacies of the seventies or eighties.

In conclusion, the host advances the thesis that in political practice the stadium has become a „lijek za sve” ("cure for everything"), and that real problems of the city are thereby neglected. This is his comment, not an analysis of the budget in the transcript.

sections.subtitle: Credit rating agencies and praise which, according to the host, hides a risk
sections.screenshot_description: On screen the logos of the credit rating agencies Moody's, Fitch and S&P, with the caption „kriza 2008.” ("crisis of 2008").
sections.content:
At 01:05:01 the host comments on the praise that Moody's gave to Croatia. He claims that this agency does not care about waste, that is, about crime and the mafia, but encourages foreign workers and facilitates their arrival in Croatia. He interprets the praise as a signal to those in power that similar moves will continue in the future.

The host recalls the role of credit rating agencies, including Moody's, Fitch and S&P, in the financial crisis of 2008. He claims that these agencies were „direktno odgovorne” ("directly responsible") for false reports and ratings, although, according to his words, they were never punished. This is his assessment, which is not supported by legal sources in the transcript.

sections.subtitle: Property tax as a cause of a potential fall in rating
sections.screenshot_description: The host speaks about property tax, with a graphic display of the credit rating.
sections.content:
At 01:06:02 the host links the credit rating agencies with the topic of property tax. He claims that these institutions are very inclined towards such a tax and that, in his opinion, they recommended it. He believes that Croatia could receive a good rating for the current situation, but that it could be lowered in the next report if the recommended measures are not implemented.

The host stresses that it is important to him to maintain a high Croatian credit rating, but emphasises that, in his opinion, it should be viewed critically. This segment reveals his suspicion of the recommendations of international agencies, without concrete data on the recommendations themselves.

sections.subtitle: Tourism, renters and the question of who profits on the Croatian coast
sections.screenshot_description: Display of a protest by entrepreneurs and a representative of renters, with the caption „19 milijuna turista” ("19 million tourists").
sections.content:
At 01:07:03 the host comments on a protest by entrepreneurs and representatives of renters. He describes that in this context Croatian entrepreneurs are „tiskaju van” ("pushing themselves out") so that foreign investors can come, which, in his opinion, means that domestic people are being squeezed out.

The host claims that, before criticism of Croatian renters as arrogant and greedy is made, a broader context should be kept in mind. He stresses that in a conflict between domestic renters and „stranih lanaca” ("foreign chains") he would take the side of the domestic ones, because foreign chains, according to his words, import everything from abroad and take most of the profit out of the country, leaving only a small tax part.

He states that 19 million tourists were recorded in Croatia this year and asks how much of that the country really benefits from, and how much it is harmed. He mentions mass tourism as a problem for a small country, but qualifies that he is not against Croatian tourism as such.

sections.subtitle: Bird flu on the Lukač farm and the question of responsibility
sections.screenshot_description: The host speaks in the frame with a shot of a farm and the caption „ptičja gripa” ("bird flu").
sections.content:
At 01:09:16 the host cites the Lukač farm as an example, where, according to his words, bird flu broke out, which led to the destruction of about 300,000 chicks. He claims that this is an event that illustrates how domestic producers can find themselves in a difficult situation. He also puts forward a guess that the disease may be a „ruska kuga” ("Russian plague") and that the chicks may have been vaccinated, which is not supported by data.

The host then links the situation with the topic of workers from abroad, who, he says, receive very low pay, while domestic workers have to fend for themselves. These claims remain at the level of the host's opinion without a source in the transcript.

sections.subtitle: Import of honey from Armenia and fear for Croatian beekeepers
sections.screenshot_description: The host reads the claims about honey imports; on screen a text with the name Armenia.
sections.content:
At 01:10:53 the host talks about the import of honey. He shows irony towards his own earlier joke that there is „nema meda” ("no honey"), but claims that Croatian honey could soon disappear as well. As a source he cites a message from EU farmers, according to which there is a danger of honey imports from third countries via Armenia, as, he says, happened with Ukrainian grain.

The host claims that this is a systematic suppression of Croatian production in favour of imports, which includes beekeepers and Slavonian pig farmers too. This part of his argument relies most on the quoted claims, but the conclusion about the intention of the Government or lobbies is not supported by further evidence in the transcript.

sections.subtitle: Language as a tool of power: from „government” to viewers' questions
sections.screenshot_description: The host speaks about the English language, with a display of viewer comments in the chat.
sections.content:
At 01:13:05 the host moves on to the topic of language. He calls English the „jezik vještica” ("language of witches") and claims that many words in it are designed to influence the mentality of speakers. As an example he cites the word „government”, which he links to a Latin root and the meaning of governing, claiming that it is a matter of mental control.

In the same segment the host reads viewers' questions and comments. He responds to them, repeating that it is hard for him to speak for three and a half hours and that some things will be repeated. This part of the show has a more relaxed tone, but still contains the host's assessments that are not supported by linguistic sources.

sections.subtitle: Foreign hotel chains and the question of where the money ends up
sections.screenshot_description: The host speaks about a planned investment in a hotel in Istria, with the caption „strani hotelski lanci” ("foreign hotel chains").
sections.content:
At 01:15:07 the host talks about the arrival of foreign hotel chains in Croatia. He claims that Croats often welcome foreign investments with enthusiasm, without thinking enough about the consequences. As an example he cites a planned investment in a hotel in Istria, which, as he says, would bring jobs, but would mainly employ workers from the Philippines and Nepal.

The host asks whether tourists will eat Croatian food, pay in Croatian currency and buy local products, and concludes that the hotel will probably not purchase food of domestic production. In this way he suggests that the profit from the investment would go out of the country.

This claim is not supported by business plans or data on money flows in the transcript, and it represents the host's assessment.

iterations.theme: European topics, US politics under Trump, wars and elections

sections.subtitle: Unrest and protests in Europe: the host sees a sign of collapse and preparation for repression
sections.screenshot_description: The host introduces the European topic with a display of street footage: burning cars, flares, mounted police and clashes near schools.
sections.content:
The host **[SPEAKER_20]** moves from topics about space and medicine to European topics. As an introduction he cites footage of large riots and protests: burning schools, smashed bars, flares, burnt cars and mounted police. He also mentions France, for which he claims that the footage showed attacks on police officers and teachers and that someone poured petrol on something. According to his words, France is preparing to strike at those who "divljaju" ("run wild").

The host does not present any verified data about the causes or scale of the unrest, but presents the protests as part of a broader picture of European instability. He announces that the next part will touch on the questions of colonialism and the situation in Europe, a topic that follows on from his depiction of Europe as a space under pressure.

For this topic it is important to note that this is a one-sided presentation based on short video clips without context. Such a way of presenting leaves viewers with an impression of chaos, without explaining the economic, political or social background of the protests.

sections.subtitle: Colonialism, foreign labour and the claim about a „slave-owner” relationship
sections.screenshot_description: The host speaks to the camera, and on screen there are captions about European colonial powers and a map of colonial empires.
sections.content:
The host links the European unrest with the concept of colonialism. He claims that European states were colonial powers for a long time, and cites the British Empire, France, Belgium and the Netherlands. In his opinion, such history is returning today as a "bumerang" ("boomerang") in the form of social tensions.

As regards Croatia, the host claims that the country was not a colonial power until 2015, but that today, as he says, it "grabi" ("grabs") workers from abroad whom it treats almost like slaves. As examples he cites workers who receive minimum earnings and accommodation, while, according to his words, priority is given to people from Ukraine and other countries. He does not cite specific sources or statistical data.

The presentation remains within the realm of commentary and the host's personal stance. The claim that foreign workers are treated as slaves is not supported in the transcript, and the comparison with colonialism is a simplification of the complex question of labour migration and the labour market.

sections.subtitle: An old illustration about the „future of France” as a prophecy: the host claims it is coming true
sections.screenshot_description: Illustration from the 1930s: people in a pool, a view of Paris and captions about the „last white French”.
sections.content:
The host shows an image which he describes as an authentic illustration from the 1930s. The poster shows, according to his description, French people in modern clothing, then scenes in a pool, and a caption speaking of the "last white French" as an attraction in Paris. The host claims that the illustration announces France 100 years from now.

When asked whether the illustration is racist, the host replies that the black people shown are "malo možda podrugljivo" ("perhaps slightly mockingly") depicted, but that the key thing is whether the author was right. He claims that the poster is "praktički pogođen" ("practically hit the mark") because, in his opinion, exactly what is depicted is happening. In doing so he does not distinguish the historical context of the poster from today's reality, and does not say who the author was or in what context it was created.

This topic shows the pattern by which the host interprets historical sources as evidence for his claims about a conspiracy and population replacement. Without a reliable origin and context, such a reading remains subjective and cannot be verified.

sections.subtitle: Trump, Ukraine and Russia: the host comments on political statements without a clear conclusion
sections.screenshot_description: Footage from a political interview or speech; on screen a caption with Trump's name and a headline about Ukraine.
sections.content:
The host announces a segment about Trump and the war in Ukraine, stating that he has neglected it until now, but that the topic is important for the European context. He shows a short excerpt in which, according to his description, Trump speaks about Ukraine and Russia. Immediately afterwards, a voice from a political interview is heard on the recording, dealing with the question of peace and cooperation with Ukraine.

In addition, the host comments that European states are under pressure from American politics and that money is being invested in military aid to Ukraine. He mentions that Germany is giving Ukraine one billion euros of military aid, but he does not cite a source or the details of that aid. The question of war aims and negotiations remains open.

The transcript shows that part of the presentation is imprecise and interrupted, so conclusions about the actual positions cannot be reliably drawn. The segment can therefore be seen as the host's commentary on the relationship between Washington, Europe and Russia, not as a verified analysis.

sections.subtitle: Refineries and American policy towards Russia: „ne gađaj rafinerije” ("don't hit the refineries") as a paradox
sections.screenshot_description: Short clip in which refineries and Russian oil are mentioned; on screen a caption about attacks on refineries.
sections.content:
In this part the host refers to the claim that Trump, in the context of the war in Ukraine, does not want Russian refineries to be attacked. In doing so he uses a metaphor about a child who must not put a finger into the dog's food, to illustrate, in his opinion, the inconsistency of American policy. According to his interpretation, Trump at the same time says that nothing may be attacked in Russia, except refineries.

The host asks what the relationship between Trump and Putin is, given that, according to his words, shortly before the recording, or in an arrangement, he heard from the Russian president. He concludes that such a policy could be interpreted as protection of Russian interests, but he does not present evidence for that conversation or for the claim about the relationship between the two leaders.

In this segment there are also interrupted statements and unclear parts of the transcript, which makes it difficult to reconstruct Trump's exact statements. Therefore the claims about the intentions and relationship of the leaders can be presented as the host's interpretation, not as a verified fact.

sections.subtitle: Claims about Trump's statements: „da nije bio predsjednik, ne bi došlo do rata” ("if he had not been president, there would have been no war")
sections.screenshot_description: Excerpt from a Trump speech; on screen the text quotes the claim that he was not president and that war would not have happened.
sections.content:
The host claims that in almost every speech about the war Trump stresses that he was president and that, if he had remained in power, there would have been no war. According to his claim, Trump has repeated this several times in the last two weeks. The host presents this claim as a pattern by which Trump presents himself as a guarantor of peace.

To check whether such a statement is true, the host announces a presentation of footage from 2024. The transcript contains no clear source for such claims, nor clearly stated dates and quotations from those speeches, so the check cannot be confirmed with certainty within this recording.

For readers it is important to distinguish Trump's public statements from the host's comments on them. A claim about repeating the same sentence requires citing specific speeches and dates in order to be verifiable.

sections.subtitle: Nord Stream: the host speaks of a „cancelled” gas pipeline and doubts about Trump's identity
sections.screenshot_description: Illustration of the Nord Stream gas pipeline and a map of the Baltic; on screen the caption „Nord Stream”.
sections.content:
In this part the host deals with the Nord Stream gas pipeline, which he describes as a project running from Russia to Germany and Europe. He claims that Trump has repeatedly boasted that he is responsible for the pipeline not being in operation, and that he admitted this in several other appearances. The host also mentions that Europe is dependent on Russia in terms of energy, and that this dependence is now presented as an American success.

To illustrate his thesis, the host shows an excerpt in which Trump appears to be speaking about the pipeline. He immediately adds that viewers might think it is a Trump double, which is an ironic comment on the doubt about the authenticity of the recordings. That claim is not supported.

To understand the topic, it is important that Nord Stream was the subject of serious political and economic disputes between the USA, Europe and Russia. The host uses this context mainly as a framework for his commentary on Europe's vassal position, so a careful check of his claims is needed.

sections.subtitle: Space and geopolitics: joint cooperation despite political conflicts
sections.screenshot_description: Footage of an international space crew; on screen flags and captions about the Antarctic Treaty and space cooperation.
sections.content:
The host returns to the topic of space in order to show that even rival states cooperate. He cites an example of members of the International Space Station, including a female astronaut from France and a Russian astronaut, and claims that political quarrels do not prevent joint work in space. He considers that such cooperation shows that this is a political spectacle.

He additionally mentions the Antarctic Treaty and joint protocols, claiming that states agree on global questions. He presents this claim without a source and without concrete examples, and presents it as his view of world politics.

The segment can be seen as an illustration of the host's conviction that public conflicts are placed in the foreground, while real cooperation is concealed. It is useful for readers to know that international cooperation in space exists, but its scope and motives require a separate analysis.

sections.subtitle: Trump and Mike Tyson in the campaign: the host sees a sports circus in politics
sections.screenshot_description: Trump and Mike Tyson on a stage or during the campaign; on screen a caption with Mike Tyson's name.
sections.content:
The host announces a segment about Trump and Mike Tyson, who appears in a political campaign. According to the recording the host comments on, Trump used sports terminology, speaking about the battle for the Senate and about having "rasprodali svaku arenu" ("sold out every arena"). The host claims that the whole political scene resembles sport, but one "namještenom" ("rigged") like professional wrestling.

As a reminder he states that Tyson appears in the political campaign in order to help mobilise voters, similar to how his performances in the past were used to attract audiences. The host also mentions that Tyson has had legal and financial problems, and that the public is interested in him again because of his appearance alongside Trump.

The exchange between celebrities and politics is presented here as a circus, not as a serious political debate. For readers it is important that all claims about motives and roles were made without full sources, so they should be read as the host's commentary.

sections.subtitle: The death penalty and public shooting: the host condemns the „culture of death”
sections.screenshot_description: The host in a recording with text about the announced public execution by firing squad in the USA.
sections.content:
The host talks about a topic which, according to his words, is currently being discussed in the USA: whether a public execution of the death penalty by shooting could take place. He mentions the case of a man who, as he says, was convicted of killing 13 or 14 American soldiers, but does not go into the details or verifiable facts of the case.

The host states that he opposes the death penalty and claims that life and death belong to God. He adds that public execution disgusts him because, as he claims, such scenes degrade society. He asks who would want to watch human dying at all, and warns of the possible mass viewership of such a broadcast.

This topic is politically and legally complex, and the host's position is expressed as a moral and religious principle. The transcript contains no concrete verified information about the current status of the case or about official American decisions, so the segment remains at the level of presenting the host's position and noting that the matter is being publicly debated.

sections.subtitle: Trump's policy towards Europe and Russian energy: „hypocrisy” ("hypocrisy") in the criticism
sections.screenshot_description: Footage from a speech or interview; on screen captions about Russian gas and energy sold to America and Europe.
sections.content:
In this section the host comments on the fact that Trump, according to his words, criticises Europe for buying Russian gas and energy, while at the same time boasting that Russian energy will come to the USA. The host claims that Trump was earlier against Russian energy in Europe, and now accepts it for America, which he sees as a contradiction.

According to the host's claim, Trump also earlier cheered on the narrative about destroying Nord Stream 2 and was against its construction. The host speaks of hypocrisy, but immediately adds that such criticism would be simplistic because, as he claims, politicians are slaves to the roles assigned to them.

The host also recalls that Croatian representatives had earlier visited Moscow and expressed gratitude to Russia, which is part of his criticism of political hypocrisy. This part is based on the host's memory, without a source in the transcript.

sections.subtitle: The height of athletes and a „conspiracy theory”: the host compares Tyson and himself
sections.screenshot_description: Shot of Mike Tyson and another person beside him; on screen a caption with heights.
sections.content:
The host presents an unusual „mala teorija zavjere” ("small conspiracy theory") about the height of Mike Tyson. He states that Tyson is officially 178 centimetres tall, but that in recordings he looks taller or that the difference cannot be seen. As a comparison he gives his own height, which he mentions as about 193 centimetres, and claims that people below 180 centimetres look considerably lower in recordings.

The host claims that in this way it could be concluded that some public figures have been replaced or that their official heights do not match reality. Such a conclusion has no support in verified data and is based on an assessment from pictures and frames.

This digression shows how the host often moves from political topics to personal and seemingly trivial examples, which then serve to raise doubts about the authenticity of public appearances.

sections.subtitle: Russian diesel and real quantities of oil: the host exposes the „sprdačina” ("fooling around") with the figures
sections.screenshot_description: Graphic with markings for 3.6 million barrels of diesel and a comparison of consumption in the USA and Europe.
sections.content:
The host deals with Trump's announcement that Russia will deliver millions of tonnes of diesel to the American and world market. He states that the agreement, which, according to his words, was verbal, concerns about 3.6 million barrels of diesel. He criticises the way Trump presented that figure as significant, and not as a relatively small quantity.

To show the scale, the host claims that such a quantity would be consumed in the USA in about ten days, and in Europe in seven days. This calculation is not shown in detail in the transcript, so it cannot be verified. The host uses it to point out that public figures are often presented in a misleading way.

Regardless of the accuracy of the calculation, the topic fits here into a broader pattern: the host doubts the way politicians present economic indicators and energy agreements.

sections.subtitle: American elections and the prospects of Republicans: the host sees the elections as a „prevara” ("fraud")
sections.screenshot_description: Graphic about the American mid-term elections for Congress and the Senate; on screen a caption about the elections and polls.
sections.content:
The host talks about the upcoming American elections, which take place at the midpoint of Trump's mandate, when Congress and part of the Senate are renewed. He claims that the elections, in his opinion, are a fraud, but also that polls often showed Republicans as losers, which, as he says, was true, but that later reversals occurred.

The host links the likely results with the political and economic situation in the USA, including American policy towards Israel, the war in Iran and fuel prices. In his opinion, such topics do not favour Republicans, which is why, as he claims, Trump is being sought a "spasitelj" ("saviour") like Tyson.

In addition, the host states that he himself once called Trump so that "Trump vratio" ("Trump would return") to power. All these claims about results and motives remain without sources and form part of the host's commentary, not verified analyses.

sections.subtitle: Technology oligarchs and Trump's administration: „tehnokratski demoni” ("technocratic demons") and universal income
sections.screenshot_description: Photographs of technology leaders (Musk, Bezos, Zuckerberg, Altman, Jensen) gathered around Trump; on screen a caption about the national medal for technology.
sections.content:
In the last part of this section the host deals with technology oligarchs who, according to his words, have gathered around Trump. He names figures such as Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos, Mark Zuckerberg, Sam Altman and Jensen Huang of Nvidia, and claims that this is a 'paralel system' ("parallel system") which oversees administration and influences state policy.

The host mentions that some technology companies received the national medal for technology and innovation, which he interprets as a sign of closeness between government and industry. He stresses that Musk entered the administration in order to reduce state spending, but that, in his opinion, American debt did not decrease.

In the closing part the host expresses concern that the introduction of universal income and digital currencies could create citizens' dependence on the state, even "totalitarizam" ("totalitarianism"). He states that citizens could, according to his words, receive money in the form of vouchers and would have no savings. According to his claim, Trump also mentioned a payment of 5,000 dollars to those who go to the polls, which the host sees as a form of political bribery. These claims are not supported in the transcript and should therefore be presented as the host's interpretation, not as a proven policy.

iterations.theme: Artificial intelligence, digital control, a children's account and closing comments

sections.subtitle: The golden promises of artificial intelligence: a cure for disease and poverty, or a new childhood illness?
sections.screenshot_description: Screen with excerpts from promotional video clips about artificial intelligence, with a heading or subtitle such as 'Obećanja i realnost' ("Promises and reality"), while the host looks into the camera.
sections.content:
In this part of the show the host refers to the promises being spread about artificial intelligence. According to his words, promotional appearances claim that technology will solve diseases and poverty, and he describes such messages as 'čudesa' ("miracles") that sound 'sve divno i krasno' ("all wonderful and nice").

**Irony towards the promises**

The host points out that, while waiting for those promised improvements, the same technology is already being used in other areas. As examples he cites surveillance of people and military technology. He presents this thesis as his own observation, without citing a source.

**'Dječje boljke' ("childhood ailments") and the path to prosperity**

At the end of the segment the host concludes that the current discomforts are in fact a passing phase. In his view, society must 'proći kroz ove stvari' ("go through these things") before it reaches prosperity. He expresses such an interpretation ironically, but at the same time uses it as an introduction to further topics about jobs and the future of work.

**The future of work: an answer without concrete answers**

The host relates a situation in which 'velikih umova' ("great minds") of the technology industry were asked what jobs would be created by replacing people with technology. According to his words, the answer was that this cannot yet be imagined, with the addition that 'nismo im ni na papiru u planu' ("we are not even on their plans on paper"). The host draws from this the thesis that people in such a perspective represent 'višak' ("surplus"), not participants in planning the future. He presents this claim as his own interpretation, not as a proven fact.

sections.subtitle: Military drones, autonomous weapons and fear of surveillance over citizens
sections.screenshot_description: Shot of drones in flight or an illustration of an autonomous drone with a caption about military technology, while the host sits in front of the camera.
sections.content:
The host links artificial intelligence with military technology. According to his words, part of the technology that is called artificial is in fact entirely controlled by people, and it deals with **surveillance of people** and **military systems**, including drones.

The segment continues with a frightening image. The host speaks about drones 'koji će nas ganjati' ("which will chase us") at the moment when someone rebels against a 'distopijski svijet' ("dystopian world"). He presents such an image as a possible scenario, not as a confirmed fact.

In the following minutes short clips from promotional materials appear on the screen, in which the defence industry and applications of technology are mentioned. The host presents this as an example of 'tehnološka optimizacija' ("technological optimisation") which is easily presented to the public as useful, although it can ultimately be used for control.

sections.subtitle: Universal basic income and digital vouchers: „wealth” without savings?
sections.screenshot_description: Screen with the title about universal basic income and a display of a digital wallet or vouchers, with the host explaining the topic.
sections.content:
The host moves on to the topic of **universal basic income** (UBI), which, according to his words, one businessman mentions in front of the American president. He describes this model as a 'turbo komunistička postavka' ("turbo-communist setup") in which citizens will receive means of subsistence from the state.

**Digital currencies as a control tool**

The host claims that digital currencies are 'sve više kucaju na vrata' ("knocking on the door more and more") precisely because such programmes would be financed in that way. According to his thesis, recipients will not have savings, but 'bonove' ("vouchers") which they must spend from month to month. From this he concludes that people will be 'sretni, a neće imati ništa' ("happy, but will have nothing").

**The paradox with Trump's stance**

The host stresses that he earlier believed that Trump strongly opposed America becoming a socialist state. Now, in his opinion, Trump has the support of the recipient of the national medal for technology and innovation, who speaks about universal high income. The host considers this a contradiction, but his conclusions remain his interpretation.

sections.subtitle: Wellness as a new business: from Roman baths to the business interests of technology giants
sections.screenshot_description: Image of a wellness centre or spa salon with a photograph of a technology director on stage, with a caption about artificial intelligence in healthcare.
sections.content:
The host comments that 'wellness' is presented as a new business trend linked to technology. According to his words, the head of the company NVIDIA, Jensen Huang, claims that wellness is a 'posao' ("business") which was non-existent during his life, but now exists.

The host responds ironically that wellness has existed as long as people have existed, citing Sumer, Egypt and Roman baths. From this he draws the thesis that it is a marketing story, not a new phenomenon.

**Business interests and the 'plan'**

The host claims that 'ti ljudi imaju plan' ("these people have a plan"), but at the same time warns about the percentage of risk that 'sve ode kvragu' ("everything goes to hell"). As an example he mentions how the same business circles spoke about this. This part remains at the level of comment and suggestion, without citing concrete evidence.

sections.subtitle: Technological 'revolution' and money: data centres and the promised 5,000 dollars
sections.screenshot_description: Excerpt from a speech by the American president in front of data centres, with a subtitle about money for citizens and companies.
sections.content:
The host comments on a speech by the American president Donald Trump about data centres. According to his words, Trump mentioned within a few minutes 47 times how much money people will receive from those centres, and also said that it is 'moralno' ("moral"). The host comments on this as a 'financijsko' ("financial") promise.

**A revolution that 'uvijek se vodi na čeg je' ("is always led on something")**

The host compares today's technological transformation with revolutions of the past and mentions Fidel Castro and the Bolsheviks. He asks whether Trump is actually a socialist, but answers himself that he probably is not. This is a rhetorical question which serves to highlight a paradox.

**Five thousand dollars for a vote**

The host also speaks about the promise that every citizen who goes to the polls and confirms their vote will receive 5,000 dollars. He points out that this may raise the question of whether it is a signed gift or a form of direct incentive to vote. The host asks why the state would distribute money at all, and concludes that such promises are a 'dar pod navodnicima' ("gift in quotation marks").

sections.subtitle: Digitalisation as a means of state control: 'cutting costs' that did not reduce debt
sections.screenshot_description: Shot of Elon Musk in a public appearance with a caption about reducing state spending and a graph of American debt.
sections.content:
The host claims that digitalisation 'samo pospješuje' ("just speeds up") the possibility for the state to have citizens 'u šaci' ("in its fist"). He links this process with the role of Elon Musk in the administration of Donald Trump, where, according to his words, he allegedly came to 'očistiti višak troškova' ("clean up excess costs") and eradicate corruption.

**Debt that did not disappear**

The host stresses that American debt, in his opinion, did not fall but even further increased. This claim is part of his criticism that 'rezanje troškova' ("cutting costs") is used as a justification for expanding control, not as real saving.

The host concludes that it is 'smiješno' ("funny") that the original justification for entering the administration, namely the debt, is now ignored while new payments to citizens are promised.

sections.subtitle: Business people in state administration and the Life Log project: the military roots of social networks
sections.screenshot_description: Archive photograph or document with the title of the Life Log project and an illustration of the Pentagon, alongside social network logos.
sections.content:
The host returns to the earlier topic of business people who perform state functions. He claims that some technology directors are in fact part of a 'paralelni sustav' ("parallel system") that shapes policy. In doing so he names Jeff Bezos, Elon Musk, Mark Zuckerberg, Sam Altman and Larry Ellison.

**Life Log and Facebook**

The host claims that the Life Log project was a Pentagon project, which, according to his words, was cancelled in 2004, and on the same day Facebook was founded. Life Log is described as a precursor of what Facebook does today: collecting information about what people do, who they spend time with and what they watch.

**The myth of the 'garage' and military roots**

The host goes on to state that both Amazon and Facebook, according to claims he says he found, originated from military projects. He mentions that the grandfather of one of the founders was a co-founder of the agency ARPA, which later became DARPA. He presents this part of his account as a 'čudna' ("strange") fact, without full evidence in the show. At the end of his comparisons, the host concludes that 'svijet postaje jedan veliki film' ("the world is becoming one big film").

sections.subtitle: Politics as a choice between bad and worse: the Club of Rome and a 'planned' collapse
sections.screenshot_description: Illustration or graph showing limited resources with the title Club of Rome, with the host pointing at the screen with his hand.
sections.content:
The host describes modern politics as a game 'između lošeg i lošijeg' ("between bad and worse"). According to his words, people no longer choose between good and bad, but between two options that are both harmful. He illustrates this impression with a comparison to the 'Gečevski show' ("Gečevski show") which the world has been attending since the late nineties.

**The Club of Rome and 'resources'**

The host refers to the Club of Rome from the sixties, which warned of catastrophes due to limited resources. According to his interpretation, all projections point to 2030 and 2040. The host claims that it is not a coincidence that we are living in precisely this period now.

**Faith and the 'planned' crisis**

The host claims that he believes that 'Bog na kraju uvijek pobjeđuje' ("God always wins in the end"), but fears that the current 'urušavanje' ("collapse") is not spontaneous but organised according to a plan. He presents this as his own opinion, without citing a source or evidence, and concludes that the world is currently preparing for 'nešto novo' ("something new").

sections.subtitle: Robots and drones in law enforcement: replacing the human factor with technology
sections.screenshot_description: Illustration of a police drone and a robotic dog, with a caption about the robotisation of law enforcement.
sections.content:
The host talks about the reasons why, according to his view, certain actors want to introduce drones and robots into law enforcement. He claims that the aim is for law enforcement officers to be as little 'ljudskog karaktera' ("human in character") as possible, and as much 'robotizirani' ("robotised") as possible.

As examples he cites drones and robotic dogs, which he describes as part of a 'distopijska' ("dystopian") future. According to his words, technology thus becomes a 'ograda' ("fence") that serves the interests of the authorities. He presents this thesis as his own interpretation of the development of technology.

sections.subtitle: The children's account announced by the American president: 'Trump account' and suspicion of fraud
sections.screenshot_description: Excerpt from a promotional video about the Trump Account with the text 'tisuću dolara za dijete' ("a thousand dollars per child"), while the host sits in front of the camera.
sections.content:
The host presents the **Trump account**, a children's account for which the American president announced that every child will receive a thousand dollars. According to the host's words, the account is opened automatically, and other payments into it remain the responsibility of parents.

**Comparison with the Israeli model**

The host claims that the programme reminds him of the Israeli model, but points out that Israelis are 'pošteniji' ("more honest") because they pay smaller amounts, but constantly. He presents such a comparison as an interesting point.

**Doubt and presentation**

The host expresses suspicion that this is a fraud and says that he cannot imagine the world in 18 years, when the child should be able to spend that money. He adds that the programme was promoted by a woman linked to the company Dell, not by the president himself, and shows an excerpt in which she explains the programme. The host stresses that he is not sure of the details, but that it 'jako smrdi na prevaru' ("smells strongly of fraud") to him.

sections.subtitle: Propaganda, images and 'visible' symbols: how the host interprets promotional materials
sections.screenshot_description: Comparison of two photographs of a woman from promotional material with an arrow pointing to a detail on her face, and a photograph of Fred Trump.
sections.content:
The host shows photographs and promotional materials and comments on them as means of propaganda. He stresses that in one of the pictures he points out a detail which 'upada u oko' ("catches his eye") and reminds him of another person. He also shows a photograph which he claims depicts Fred Trump, the father of the American president, with the note that 'nije riječ o AI-u' ("it is not about AI").

**Comments on the presentation and 'change' of appearance**

The host claims that the images were manipulated and that a change in the appearance of a public figure can be seen in them, which, according to him, raises the question of what happened. This part contains a series of assumptions and suggestions, which the host does not support with official sources.

**Gestures and 'signs'**

The host claims that people were forced to make a certain hand gesture, and as an example he cites the difference between the so-called 'Devil's horns' sign and the gesture made by the pope. From this he draws the thesis about a symbolic meaning, which he presents as his own opinion.

sections.subtitle: Football conspiracy theories: tattoos, appearance and doubts about a player being swapped
sections.screenshot_description: Side-by-side photograph of a footballer with tattoos before and after the World Cup, with a headline about doubts over a player being replaced.
sections.content:
The host moves on to a football topic and presents theories about a footballer who, according to claims in circulation, became different after jaw surgery. The host shows comparative pictures and claims that the tattoos on the leg and arm disappeared or changed after the World Cup.

**Analysis without confirmation**

The host considers the possibility that the player 'smršavio' ("lost weight") and that his skin colour changed, but at the same time admits that he is not sure of the conclusion. He stresses that he cannot rule out any possibility, adding that he 'ne uzima ništa zdravo za gotovo' ("does not take anything for granted").

**Broader conclusion**
