The host claims that everything 'se poklapa' ("matches up") and that such 'slučajnosti' ("coincidences") are so frequent that he cannot explain them by chance. He presents this thesis as his own interpretation, without evidence from official sources.

sections.subtitle: The host's tiredness and viewers' comments: a show lasting almost three hours
sections.screenshot_description: The host shows a screen with the live chat and the number of viewers, and tiredness is visible on his face.
sections.content:
The host openly admits that he feels tired, because the show lasts almost three hours. He explains that the preparation took him the whole day and that 'zamor materijala' ("material fatigue") is beginning to affect his energy.

**Reading comments**

The host then reads viewers' comments in the chat. Among them are greetings and questions, and one viewer comments that he 'zakucao do kraja' ("hammered it to the end"). The host thanks the viewers and announces a short break.

**Proposal for continuation**

At the end of the part the host stresses that he could speak for a long time, but wonders how much 'žara' ("fire" or "passion") there would be in that speech. He announces that he will continue for a little while longer, thanking viewers for their patience.

sections.subtitle: Water quality, pollution and criticism of the authorities: from Zagreb to Našice
sections.screenshot_description: Display of a water filter and a card with a note about pollution in Zagreb and Našice, with the host reading a viewer's comment.
sections.content:
The host comments on water quality and air pollution. He reads a comment from a viewer from Split who states that after the autumn rains the water is sometimes not drinkable, so he intends to buy filters. The host comments that Croatia likes to boast of clean waters and nature, but that 'gamad i mafija' ("vermin and mafia") are endangering that.

**Smell in Zagreb and Našice**

The host mentions the mysterious smell that was felt in Zagreb for several days. In addition he cites fires in recycling yards and landfills in Našice and stresses that he links such fires with climate change and poor waste management.

**Waste from Gospić and criticism of the authorities**

The host claims that waste from Gospić is 'već u cementari' ("already in the cement plant") and states that this is a decision of the Government which, according to his words, 'nema adekvatno mjesto' ("has no adequate place") for incineration. He also criticises the attitude of the authorities towards citizens' health, presenting all of this with irony and sarcastic comments.

**Link with waste and activism**

The host mentions a video he published, in which a female interlocutor speaks about waste. According to his words, that video has over 30,000 views.

sections.subtitle: Illegal waste and activism: the story of a man who confronted a lorry
sections.screenshot_description: Photograph or archive recording of an activist in front of a lorry with waste, with a headline about illegal dumping.
sections.content:
The host talks about the illegal dumping of waste in Croatia and recalls an example of an activist who, according to his words, confronted a lorry carrying hazardous waste. According to his description, the man stood in front of the lorry at a landfill that was not intended for that waste, after which he was arrested.

**Comparison with football events**

The host links that story with the protest in Split over the transfer of the footballer Kranjčar from Dinamo to Hajduk. According to his words, more than several thousand people were at the protest, while at the same time there were only a few activists at the stopping of the lorry. He uses this contrast to emphasise the disproportion of attention paid to different topics.

sections.subtitle: Comment on an incident on an aircraft: the 'hero' and doubts about the official story
sections.screenshot_description: Illustration of a passenger aircraft in flight from Dubai towards Israel, with a headline about an incident involving a passenger.
sections.content:
The host announces a comment on an incident on an aircraft which was flying from Dubai towards Israel. According to his words, he prepared a special contribution about the event, but in the end does not plan to show it in full.

The host claims that the passenger who declared himself a hero allegedly saved the plane because he had watched investigations of air crashes. At the same time he claims that the passenger lied about how he fought with the cockpit door, stating that the doors 'otvaraju na van' ("open outwards"). The host concludes sarcastically that if the passenger came from the Israeli service, one 'mora' ("has to") believe that he is telling the truth.

The host presents this comment in the form of an ironic observation, without citing official sources or confirmed facts about the event.

sections.subtitle: Thanks to subscribers and farewell to viewers: support for the channel as 'fuel'
sections.screenshot_description: The host says goodbye to viewers, and on screen there is a message of thanks and a subscriber counter.
sections.content:
At the end of the show the host thanks viewers and subscribers who support the channel. He mentions that the show had over a thousand live viewers and that many of them took part in funding through payments and subscriptions.

**Support as a precondition for work**

The host explains that viewers' support enables him to devote himself to the channel full-time. He stresses that part of these funds is 'gorivo' ("fuel") that gives him time to prepare topics. He also notes that his life circumstances are changing and that he might have to work on something else if his financial situation changes.

**Farewell**

The host addresses his closing words to viewers, thanks them for their patience and announces that they will see each other again at some future gathering. The show ends with his greeting.
